newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian crudes firm as Gulf grades take off.
newsitem.headline: Asian crudes firm as Gulf grades take off.

text.p: Wet crude trading of Gulf grades in Asia took off on Friday with premiums firming strongly and two U.S. majors seen as featured buyers.
Traders said the Gulf crude traded was destined for Japan on the basis the light Gulf grades represent best value.
"If you can handle the sulphur, they are the grades you will buy," one trader said.
Murban traded several times up to a premium over ADNOC of 55 cents per barrel. The two U.S. majors were the main buyers.
Lower Zakum traded a few times with a deal as high as ADNOC +63 cents per barrel.
Umm Shaif also traded a few times and the highest price achieved was ADNOC +67 cents per barrel.
Qatar Land traded at QGPC +27.5 cents and +30 cents.
Traders said four cargos of Qatar Marine traded at premiums ranging from +31 to +36 cents, with Thailand a noted buyer.
Traders said the premiums achieved were sharply higher than for November barrels and reflected in the case of the U.S. majors a late need to cover for December requirements.
A European major sold an Oman cargo to another European major at MPM +7 cents -- the highest level for Oman cargos.
However, one of the players involved said there were special conditions to the deal, although adding that the paid price was in line with the market.
Traders said a November Belida had traded at a premium over ICP of $1.30 -- in line with its rival Tapis values.
Dubai intermonth quotes were steady at 50/55 cents for near months ahead of the Indian tender which is expected to be awarded this weekend.
Traders said six Dubai cargoes had been offered at prices ranging 57 to 63 cents over first half November quotes.
